Exhibits so many of the One Autodesk attributes
One Autodesk. Great at focusing on what the outcome is and bringing people together to solve it. Passionate about the company and the mission. Saw that when he took on the ideal user work
Optimistic. Very solutions and execution focused. Doesn't just talk about things but executes - Formaverse. Also shows a true growth mindset, with great curiosity and willingness to share
Relentless. Showed ability to adjust and change focus based on feedback as I saw when we discussed outputs from the ideal user work. Able to prioritse and bring great urgency

Trusted. Danniel goes the extra mile to deliver. He is super reliable. I don't need to follow-up . Willing to raise challenges and concerns. Quality of work is really high.

column8: The WHAT: How has this individual made an impact and delivered results for your project/team/customers this year? Provide 1-2 specific examples.
column9:
Domain knowledge. Daniel has excellent domain knowledge, but most importantly he has been very willing to share and answer lots of 'stupid' questions from me and other members of the team
Focus. He has shown a brilliant ability to focus on impact, despite wanting a new challenge. He is super reliable in terms of doing what he says and 100% committed to doing the best job he can
Forma Verse. Great example of identifying a problem and being relentless to solving it. Great example of self learning - couldn't code to building a full stack application.
Ideal user. Took an initial workshop output and turned it into a valuable piece of work with minimal guidance needed. Worked closely with other team members to deliver an excellent results
Street Design. Working with the Site Design team, Daniel did an excellent piece of discovery work. He spoke with users, did analysis and build a very strong understanding of the problem and solution space. 
Proactiveness. Daniel recognised that we weren't making the progress we wanted with Community. He was creative in coming up with a strategy to improve - running vibe coding event. Look on feedback to improve it too.

column8: What might help this person be more effective in the WHAT and/or the HOW? Provide 1-2 specific examples. Don't forget to consider the One ORBIT Autodesk Culture Guide
column9:
Both areas below are already areas Daniel is cognicent of and improving on. I want to emphasize that they are relatively minor points. 

Optimistic – One area Daniel can continue to refine is expanding his marketing knowledge. He’s already been open to learning and proactive, and deepening that understanding will help him embed even more effectively within the team. This will also strengthen his ability to align his creative initiatives with broader marketing strategies.

Brave – Daniel is aware that his direct communication style can occasionally cause a little friction in meetings or brainstorming sessions. While his strong opinions are valuable, continuing to fine-tune how he shares them will ensure that all colleagues feel heard and that discussions remain collaborative. Encouraging him to remain mindful of tone and delivery will help maintain the positive, open environment he contributes to.

Ingenious – Daniel demonstrates a strong focus on data and continuous improvement. He blends experimentation with a clear eye on OKRs, ensuring that every new approach is tied to meaningful outcomes. He’s taken feedback well and moves quickly to deliver results, like turning a "Vibe coding" webinar concept into reality within two weeks.

Optimistic – He’s also done a great job championing his own work in a positive and non-arrogant way. By sharing his successes in forums like the Forma Forward steerco or Friday Wins meetings, he’s increased his visibility and contributed to team morale.

column8: The WHAT: How has this individual made an impact and delivered results for your project/team/customers this year? Provide 1-2 specific examples.
column9:
Ingenious – Daniel consistently brings a creative and motivated approach to his work. He introduces new technologies and learns quickly, whether it’s experimenting with new tools or applying a product manager mindset to community amplification. For example, at AU, he took the initiative to meet with class leaders to help them enhance their social media presence, resulting in a 2.5x increase in community impressions.

Relentless – He also launched the FormaVerse, a vibe coded website for managing open data assets, which has already driven over 1,000 downloads. He’s constantly thinking about how to refine and expand these experiments to generate more community-driven content. He holds himself accountable on the results and KPIs.

column9: Daniel tends to prioritize speed, which works well in early stages but limits how broadly his work scales. column8: The WHAT: How has this individual made an impact and delivered results for your project/team/customers this year? Provide 1-2 specific examples.
column9:
Daniel accelerated my adoption of Cursor massively. He embraced the tool early, went deep on understanding it, and helped me get productive far faster than I would have on my own. His MVP work—especially the demo used for user interviews—shows how quickly he can turn ideas into something testable.
Our weekly sessions helped me learn how to structure PRDs for MVP validation, set up a workable coding environment, and follow best practices for building in Lovable and Cursor. 
Additionally while working on workshops he has drawn me in for support on user profiles and he manages a wide scope well to produce a result quite fast.

column9:
In my view, Daniel consistently shows up as Trusted and Relentless.
- Trusted: Daniel delivers on workstreams assigned to him, speaks with authority on user experience and AEC matters and demonstrates empathy and inclusion which makes collaborators bring their best work. He clearly communicates his capacity and expectations, and informs collaborators early when priorities shift.
- Relentless: Daniel stays on task until the outcome is delivered, while staying open and flexible to other ways of delivering the outcome. He delegates well, shares expectations clearly and follows up at the right frequency to drive progress.

column8: The WHAT: How has this individual made an impact and delivered results for your project/team/customers this year? Provide 1-2 specific examples.
column9:
Daniel led the work to deliver and socialize the Ideal User Profile. This is a key part of the PLG framework and was a missing piece of our GTM efforts. 

As always, he has made it easy to contribute to the effort, by setting clear outcomes and expectations, understanding what work is best progressed async or in meetings, escalated when necessary and facilitated workshops in a way that got all participant's knowledge and points included. He has also led the effort to socialize this work with the wider org, to maximize the impact. This subsequently made it easier for Growth to collaborate with PMs in core on FSMs and Target users. 

In addition, he has developed and implemented the Formaverse, revamped efforts to get more out of our LinkedIn presence, made data and experimentation core to the community efforts and delivered discovery and scoping of the business opportunity of adding engineers as a Target User in Site Design. After being on parental leave for most of H1.

column8: The HOW: What behavior strengths did this person demonstrate consistently this year? Provide 1-2 specific examples. Don't forget to consider the One ORBIT Autodesk Culture Guide
column9:
1. RELENTLESS. Daniel collaborated with me on estimating the opportunity size for the current Forma offering and FCC workflows. The delivery time deadline was too short to accommodate the needs of collaborating cross-functionally (with ACS analysts), and to verify everything. Despite that, Daniel demonstrated support and continued interest in getting the right results, even if beyond the deadline, because he was consistent and thorough in his ask and rationale. 
2. TRUST. To continue on the same idea as above, Daniel showed me that he was invested in the task force at a profound level, not doing it superficially, just to check a box of "being data driven" and "delivering a task force". He invested time and thinking power in partnering with me and this gained my trust in him, as well as it made me feel that my expertise is valuable. The ask was complex and he delivered on the commitment made to me to solve it, even if it took longer and several iterations.

column8: The WHAT: How has this individual made an impact and delivered results for your project/team/customers this year? Provide 1-2 specific examples.
column9:
1. Task forces leadership and outstanding delivery. Daniel stands out for gathering his resources and enabling others to do the same and create task forces (TFs) that are delivering a significant impact of the organisation he's part of. In the past it was the workflows, as an example, and more recently, the ideal user profile (IUP). He manages to lead the team to delivery on time, based on deep work, and within scope.
2. Industry expertise. Daniel's background in architecture as well as the long tenure in the team, varying several different roles, enables him to not only contribute with delivering results by himself, but also with enabling others with direction towards the most productive and impactful contributions. By himself, in the IUP TF, Daniel formulated hypothesis on slicing the groups of users. By enabling others, he offered structure and a clear scope, guidance to follow it and avoid scope creep, and a continuous thinking partnership.
3. Data driven. Daniel is data driven in a way that I wish more leaders at higher levels demonstrate to be. He pushed for getting data about usage of other products so that he is backed by data when estimating the opportunity size for the current Forma offering and FCC workflows.
